chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has days of the month of Ramadan remaining on him, should he make them up separately? He said, 'There is no harm in separating the making up of the month of Ramadan; rather, the fasting that must not be separated is the expiation for Zad (verbal divorce), the expiation for blood, and the expiation for an oath.'

key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up missed fasts of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Can missed Ramadan fasts be made up individually or must they be consecutive?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the distinction is drawn between the general obligation of Qada (making up missed Ramadan fasts) and specific expiations (Kaffarah) that require consecutive fasting, such as for Zad or breaking an oath. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing believers to fulfill their Ramadan debt individually without the strict continuity required for penitential acts. The hadith underscores the principle that unless explicitly mandated by text, religious obligations do not impose unnecessary hardship regarding the sequence of performance.
